results.title: Exploring the Feasibility and Performance of Distributed Llm Serving on Consumer-Grade Gpus
results.venue: IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems
results.abstract: The advances in large language models come with a challenge: the high cost of model serving. Consumer-grade GPUs emerge as a cost-efficient alternative. However, there remains a gap in the systematic study of their feasibility and performance. In this work, we present the first comprehensive study of LLM serving on consumer-grade GPUs. We characterize serving performance using six representative benchmarks and uncover four key findings that are often masked in traditional datacentercentric studies: (1) Consumer-grade GPUs offer low latency inference but suffer from low concurrency due to limited memory. (2) Tensor parallelism does not always provide benefits due to PCIe bandwidth constraints. Switching to pipeline parallelism can mitigate this issue. (3) Scaling pipeline parallelism yields superlinear throughput gains, but these gains diminish under lower network bandwidth. (4) State-of-the-art serving systems suffer from two typical limitations: (i) prefill requests blocking decode requests, and (ii) underutilized memory in heterogeneous hardware settings. To address these limitations, we propose two simple yet effective techniques. Experiments show that our approach reduces Time to First Token (TTFT) by up to 37.82%, Time Per Output Token (TPOT) by up to 18.72%, and improves overall throughput by up to $\mathbf{2 1. 8 6 \%}$ compared to the baselines. Furthermore, it achieves up to $\mathbf{1 1. 2 \%}$ higher throughput in heterogeneous settings.
